oregon-sues-openai-for-2-billion-over-ch.title: Oregon Sues OpenAI for $2 Billion Over Child Safety Concerns
oregon-sues-openai-for-2-billion-over-ch.one_liner: California and Oregon filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI citing AI safety concerns and risks to children from ChatGPT.

openai-launches-gpt-62-astra-and-sol-wit.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with Risk Ratings
openai-launches-gpt-62-astra-and-sol-wit.one_liner: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on 17 November 2026. Astra is the flagship model for demanding projects; Sol is a cheaper model for routine work. Astra's API prices are $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, representing a 20% reduction from GPT-6 Astra. Sol maintains the $2 and $10 rates of GPT-6.1 Sol. On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark, Astra outscores GPT-6 Astra by 5.2 points while costing under a third as much per task, and edges Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 points. Astra's documents, spreadsheets and slide decks follow professional conventions in law, finance and accounting more closely. An Astra for Law variant launched the same day, now available to ChatGPT Enterprise customers via OpenAI's Trusted Access Program; on the Harvey LAB-AA legal benchmark it earned full marks on 20.8% of assignments versus 15.0% for standard GPT-6.2 Astra. Both models meet Critical cybersecurity thresholds and High bars for bio and chemical risk. GPT-6.2 Astra is the first model OpenAI has released externally that reaches High rating for AI self-improvement under its Preparedness Framework. OpenAI describes this High rating as roughly equivalent to providing each of its researchers an extra highly capable research engineer compared to a 2024 baseline. In response, OpenAI has strengthened containment safeguards on high-risk cyber requests and built a system called Control Room to halt model output on research workloads. Both models were more likely than GPT-6 Astra to stay silent about obstacles preventing task completion in two alignment tests.

california-cybersecurity-firm-uses-opena.title: California cybersecurity firm uses OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber to identify critical Java vulnerability
california-cybersecurity-firm-uses-opena.one_liner: California cybersecurity firm Calif disclosed on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, that it used OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model to identify a critical software vulnerability in Java. Java is used by government agencies and approximately 90% of Fortune 500 companies across banking, health care, aviation, and technology sectors. Calif senior researcher Bruce Dang stated the vulnerability could affect nearly all major companies. The company coordinated the disclosure with government agencies in the Five Eyes countries (the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom) and contacted major private-sector providers including Google and Microsoft. A classified network at the U.S. National Security Agency went offline on Tuesday for what the agency described as routine software maintenance; the NSA did not confirm whether the outage was related to the Java vulnerability.

openai-releases-gpt-62-with-astra-and-so.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 with Astra and Sol models
openai-releases-gpt-62-with-astra-and-so.one_liner: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, 2026. Both models are designed for coding tasks and code review, with improved performance compared to earlier GPT-6 models. GPT-6.2 Astra caught significantly more issues in code review than GPT-6 Astra while using fewer tokens for agentic coding and terminal work. GPT-6.2 Sol caught nearly twice as many real issues in code review as GPT-6.1 Sol while maintaining accuracy; on Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, Sol came within half a point of Astra at approximately one-fifth the cost. Both models are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users across Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, github.com, GitHub Mobile, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, and Eclipse. The $200/month Pro plan now includes Ultrafast mode for Sol; the $500/month Pro plan includes Ultrafast for both models. Ultrafast can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate. Astra's standard pricing is 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra; Sol maintains GPT-6.1 pricing. Both models are available through the API. Rollout is gradual; Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators can manage model access through Copilot settings.

rare-immune-disorder-breakthrough-points.title: Rare Immune Disorder Breakthrough Points to New Treatment
rare-immune-disorder-breakthrough-points.one_liner: Scientists at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have discovered that mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), a rare genetic inflammatory disorder affecting hundreds of children and adults worldwide, is driven by malfunctioning natural killer (NK) immune cells rather than macrophages as previously believed for three decades. MKD causes recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and abdominal inflammation, with the most severe episodes potentially life-threatening. The researchers found that NK cells in MKD patients fail to mature properly and cannot destroy infected cells, causing them to release excessive amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, particularly interferon gamma, which triggers widespread inflammation. The study, published in Immunity journal on November 18, 2026, points to a treatment using existing JAK inhibitor medications to neutralize interferon gamma. This approach could benefit the approximately 50 percent of MKD patients who do not respond adequately to current therapies targeting macrophage signals. One severely affected infant has already shown substantial improvement with the new treatment approach. Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author, described this as a new target for the inflammatory disorder that sets the stage for future clinical studies.

magnetic-nanoparticles-show-promise-for-.title: Magnetic nanoparticles show promise for less-invasive Parkinson's treatment
magnetic-nanoparticles-show-promise-for-.one_liner: Scientists at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), RWTH Aachen, and the Universities of Maastricht and Leuven demonstrated that injectable magnetic nanoplatelets can stimulate deep brain regions to improve Parkinson's-like movement problems in mice without permanently implanted electrodes. The technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted brain area; when exposed to external magnetic fields, these particles generate tiny mechanical forces that activate nearby nerve cells. The approach targets the subthalamic nucleus (STN), the same region treated by conventional deep brain stimulation devices (brain pacemakers). Unlike current treatments that require surgical implantation of electrodes beneath the collarbone, the magnetic nanoparticle method uses non-implanted external magnetic fields to influence brain activity. The findings were published in Advanced Science. Researchers suggest the approach could eventually enable treatment using injectable particles and wearable magnetic headbands, potentially offering an alternative for Parkinson's patients who are not suitable candidates for or refuse conventional brain pacemaker surgery.

nvidia-leadership-transition-underway-as.title: Nvidia leadership transition underway as CEO Huang exits
nvidia-leadership-transition-underway-as.one_liner: Nvidia's board has confirmed CEO Jensen Huang's departure is permanent, with board chair Harvey Jones stating the board 'unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.' Huang left 'under a cloud' the previous week. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress is leading the company while the board engages executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. In Q3 earnings, Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion (103 percent increase year-over-year) and operating income of $77.5 billion (115 percent increase). Kress raised the company's fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70 percent to 75 percent, citing growing demand and additional supply. The board is strengthening oversight by creating a committee to scrutinize security policies and export compliance. Analysts expressed concerns about operational risks, including maintaining employee confidence, retaining talent, and preserving innovation culture during the leadership transition, despite strong near-term demand.

russian-apt-exploits-stolen-identities-t.title: Russian APT exploits stolen identities to breach US organization after prior compromise
russian-apt-exploits-stolen-identities-t.one_liner: Russia-linked APT Star Blizzard (also tracked as Callisto, Cold Relic, Cold River, UNC4057, and Gossamer Bear) breached a US organization by impersonating an employee of another US organization it had previously compromised. The first organization was hit in late 2025 using compromised credentials of a super admin account; Star Blizzard exploited MFA push notification fatigue to register a device to the victim's tenant. During that initial intrusion, the group downloaded the organization's entire cloud storage drive, accessed the admin console to fingerprint defenses and remove evidence, exported full employee lists, launched a domain-wide export, and exfiltrated emails and targeted cloud drive documents. The group used passkeys, rogue MFA devices, and MFA backup codes to maintain persistent access for several months. Star Blizzard then weaponized contact and relationship information obtained during the earlier intrusion to select and phish a separate US target by impersonating an employee of the first breached organization. Star Blizzard is formally associated by the US with Russia's FSB intelligence service and has been active for over a decade, known for targeting high-value victims including government officials, defense contractors, and NGOs across Europe and North America.

new-tpm-attack-breaks-windows-hello-and-.title: New TPM Attack Breaks Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs
new-tpm-attack-breaks-windows-hello-and-.one_liner: Researchers at Technische Universität Berlin discovered a hardware-level vulnerability affecting TPM (Trusted Platform Module) lockout mechanisms on AMD-based PCs and some Intel PCs. By physically opening the PC case and accessing the mainboard's flash chip, attackers can reset the TPM lockout counter that protects Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs from brute-force guessing. In laboratory tests, researchers cracked a four-digit Windows Hello PIN in 57 minutes (236 attempts) and a six-digit BitLocker PIN in 6 minutes 55 seconds (236 attempts). Without the lockout mechanism, worst-case attack times drop dramatically: a four-digit Hello PIN from 69 days to 40 hours; a six-digit BitLocker PIN from 19 years to 20 days. The vulnerability stems from two separate weaknesses depending on hardware configuration. On AMD PCs using RPMC (Replay Protected Monotonic Counter) counters, the processor firmware fails to verify that counters actually increased, allowing an interposer board to block updates and report false success. On systems with Winbond flash chips, a voltage glitch attack can extract the secret key that signs counter values in approximately one second, enabling forgery of any counter value. AMD confirmed the processor firmware flaw and plans fixes for most affected chips between November 2026 and February 2027. Microsoft's documented lockout policy locks the TPM after 32 wrong PIN attempts with a 10-minute delay between failures, but this protection is bypassed by resetting the counter. Researchers advised temporarily adding at least two digits to Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs as mitigation.

nvidia-halts-advanced-ai-chip-shipments-.title: Nvidia Halts Advanced AI Chip Shipments to China
nvidia-halts-advanced-ai-chip-shipments-.one_liner: Nvidia has halted shipments of its advanced H200 (Hopper architecture) AI chips to China, reversing a decision made after the company received White House approval to export the processors in December 2025. Interim CEO Colette Kress announced the cessation during an earnings call on November 18, 2026, stating: "Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China." Kress did not publicly explain the reason for the reversal or whether Nvidia would pursue other business dealings with China. The shift marks a notable turnaround from the previous efforts under former CEO Jensen Huang, who had advocated for approval to sell the H200 chips to China. Huang resigned from his CEO position the week prior following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.

2026-himalayan-glacial-collapse-killed-h.title: 2026 Himalayan glacial collapse killed hundreds in Nepal-Tibet border region
2026-himalayan-glacial-collapse-killed-h.one_liner: On August 26, 2026, the lower section of the Langtang Lirung Glacier collapsed at an altitude of 5,200 meters in the Himalayan region along the Nepal-Tibet border. The glacier break triggered a cascade of ice, rock, and debris that swept down the valley floor to approximately 3,800 meters, generating massive landslides and catastrophic flash floods downstream. The collapse killed at least 162 people in Nepal according to police reports, with China's Xinhua News Agency reporting 3 dead in Tibet as of August 27. Approximately 1,000 people remained missing across both regions: Nepal reported 403 missing (including 341 foreigners), while Tibet reported 558 missing (including 260 foreigners and 2 villagers rescued). The U.S. Geological Survey determined that what was initially suspected to be an earthquake in the region was in fact seismic energy generated by the collapse itself, followed by debris flow. Satellite imagery from August 24 (before) and August 26 (after) confirmed the glacier break. The disaster occurred in Nepal's Nuwakot district and surrounding areas; communities were given little warning, with floods arriving within hours. The incident represents the second major glacial-flood event in the Lhende Khola river system within 14 months, following similar floods in August 2025 that killed 9 people.

critical-perforce-puppet-rce-vulnerabili.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Vulnerability CVE-2026-115731 Actively Exploited
critical-perforce-puppet-rce-vulnerabili.one_liner: A critical remote code execution vulnerability in Perforce Puppet tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.4) is being actively exploited. The vulnerability is a deserialization of untrusted data issue in the report processing of Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core that allows clients holding a certificate signed by the Puppet certificate authority to send reports with malicious payloads executed on the server with service user permissions. A successful attack could expose the server's certificate-signing key, allow issuance of trusted certificates, and enable changes to software and configuration delivered to managed systems. The flaw was patched on November 3 alongside CVE-2026-115732. Patched versions include Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Enterprise Advanced 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1, and 2023.8.13, and Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2. The vulnerability was flagged as exploited on November 4. The US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 17, urging federal agencies to patch within two weeks per BOD 26-04. The vulnerability also affects OpenVox configuration management platform. Administrators are advised to disable auto-signing of certificate requests and enforce strong validation.

xi-greets-the-president-of-the-united-st.title: Xi Greets the President of the United States Upon Arrival in China Before Putin Talks
xi-greets-the-president-of-the-united-st.one_liner: On November 18, 2026, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted the president of the United States upon his arrival in Shenzhen, China. The greeting on the tarmac is believed to be the first time Xi has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China during his more than a decade in power. Xi's move reciprocated a personal greeting the president of the United States had extended to him in September when Xi arrived for a White House state visit at Joint Base Andrews. The greeting preceded scheduled trilateral talks involving the president of the United States, Xi, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Upon disembarking from Air Force One, the two leaders shook hands, which turned into a quick hug. Military regiments and performers in bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention, with a martial band playing the American and Chinese national anthems while dancers waved flowers, pompoms, and both nations' flags. Xi cited China's tradition of "returning goodwill with goodwill" in reference to the president of the United States' September greeting. Analysts noted the gesture likely reflects a desire to show respect to the president of the United States and to maintain positive rapport ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations.

putin-arrives-in-asia-with-deployment-of.title: Putin Arrives in Asia With Deployment of Nuclear-Capable Bombers as Military Show of Force
putin-arrives-in-asia-with-deployment-of.one_liner: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit on November 18, 2026, coinciding with a significant Russian military aircraft deployment across East Asia. Two Tu-95 strategic bombers (NATO designation "Bears"), some of which are nuclear-capable, flanked by two long-range tanker aircraft, landed at Danang airport in Vietnam on Wednesday, November 17. The bombers had flown south from Russia's Far East on Tuesday, alerting air forces in Taiwan and Japan. This marked Russia's most substantial strategic airpower deployment to East Asia in over a decade—the last known deployment of Russian strategic aircraft to Vietnam occurred in 2012-2014, when Moscow used Cam Ranh Bay and Danang airfield for Tu-95 flights and tanker operations. Moscow had requested to revive such arrangements last year but faced initial Vietnamese hesitancy. The November 2026 deployment, ostensibly for refueling, signals a shift in approach and may herald further operations. Experts assess the deployment as intended to demonstrate Moscow's continued power projection capability in Southeast Asia despite the Ukraine war, and as a potent message ahead of concurrent US-China-Russia diplomatic engagement (the president of the United States was gathered in Manila for ASEAN meetings). The Tu-95s are sometimes deployed for intelligence gathering and surveillance operations.

breakthrough-electron-pairs-found-at-roo.title: Breakthrough: Electron Pairs Found at Room Temperature, May Enable Superconductors
breakthrough-electron-pairs-found-at-roo.one_liner: Scientists from Utrecht, Leiden, and Munich discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood—a critical requirement for superconductivity that can now occur at room temperature. The finding, published in Science, suggests that electron pairing is not the obstacle preventing room-temperature superconductivity; instead, a different mechanism is holding it back. Conventional superconductors require cooling to approximately -260°C (liquid helium temperatures). High-temperature superconductors discovered in the mid-1980s function around -173°C, but their underlying mechanism remains poorly understood and cannot be explained by the theory governing conventional superconductivity. The breakthrough indicates that achieving room-temperature superconductivity may be possible if researchers can identify and overcome the remaining barrier beyond electron pairing.

change-4-and-change-6-reveal-postimpact-.title: Chang'e-4 and Chang'e-6 Reveal Postimpact Evolution of South Pole–Aitken Basin
change-4-and-change-6-reveal-postimpact-.one_liner: China's Chang'e-6 mission retrieved the first samples from the lunar farside South Pole–Aitken basin, the Moon's largest impact basin. Analysis reveals the basin's three-layer differentiated structure formed by massive crust–mantle reorganization: 51% dunite, 44% norite, and 5% orthopyroxenite. Lunar regolith penetrating radar also revealed subsurface structure at the southwestern Apollo basin landing site showing distinct two-layer composition to 3 meters depth.
takeaways: South Pole–Aitken basin: 51% dunite, 44% norite, 5% orthopyroxenite composition
Basin melt sheet shows 20–30% highland crustal contribution to mantle source
Radar revealed two-layer regolith structure: ~1.7 m fine-grained weathered layer, lower coarse unweathered ejecta
Apollo basin site approximately 2.79 billion years old

single-cell-long-noncoding-rna-atlas-rev.title: Single-Cell Long Noncoding RNA Atlas Reveals Pan-Cancer Tumor Microenvironment Programs
single-cell-long-noncoding-rna-atlas-rev.one_liner: Researchers published an integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) atlas analyzing 219,442 potential lncRNAs across 13 cancer types using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. The study identified 94,795 previously unannotated lncRNAs and validated findings across seven cancer types using multiple sequencing platforms. A cloud-based database called SPanC-Lnc was built on AWS to enable discovery of functional lncRNAs in tumor microenvironments.
takeaways: 219,442 potential lncRNAs analyzed across 13 cancer types
94,795 previously unannotated lncRNAs identified
Validation across 7 cancer types using 3 spatial transcriptomics platforms and 2 long-read sequencing methods
Free cloud-based SPanC-Lnc database on AWS for lncRNA discovery

hydrogen-radical-participating-spatiotem.title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
hydrogen-radical-participating-spatiotem.one_liner: Researchers developed a novel cancer therapy combining hydrogen radical participation with hypoxia aggravation to amplify immunotherapy effects.

somatostatin-6-as-master-maternal-mrna-d.one_liner: Scientists identified somatostatin 6 as a critical maternal mRNA regulating early embryonic development.

openai-models-advance-semiconductor-chip.title: OpenAI models advance semiconductor chip design
openai-models-advance-semiconductor-chip.one_liner: OpenAI and Synopsys announced a multi-year strategic partnership on September 30, 2026, to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized AI model for semiconductor chip design. The model combines OpenAI's frontier capabilities with Synopsys' electronic design automation tools and can iteratively optimize designs for power, performance, area, timing, and verification without requiring manual tool operation.
takeaways: Partnership announced September 30, 2026
GPT-Synopsys combines OpenAI AI with Synopsys EDA tools
Model learns to operate tools, interpret outputs, and optimize designs iteratively
Revenue-sharing arrangement; runs on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure

openais-gpt-6-cyber-detects-35-vulnerabi.one_liner: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model identified approximately 35 security vulnerabilities across Apple's product line (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro) in collaboration with cybersecurity firm Calif. Some flaws could allow attackers to hijack devices through malicious websites. GPT-6 Cyber was unveiled November 5, 2026, and discovers vulnerabilities twice as fast as GPT-6.1 Sol but at higher cost.

nih-to-relocate-its-last-research-chimpa.title: NIH to relocate its last research chimpanzees to sanctuary next year
nih-to-relocate-its-last-research-chimpa.one_liner: The National Institutes of Health will transfer nearly three dozen chimpanzees from the Keeling Center for Comparative Medicine and Research in Texas to Chimp Haven sanctuary in Louisiana beginning early 2027. This move fulfills the NIH's November 2015 commitment to retire all NIH-owned chimpanzees to sanctuary and ends federal research use of the species.

Nearly three dozen chimpanzees from Keeling Center (Bastrop, Texas)
Fulfills November 2015 NIH commitment to retire all federal chimpanzees
Ends federal research use of chimpanzees

disabling-cellular-recycling-increases-p.title: Disabling cellular recycling increases pharmaceutical protein production 57-fold
disabling-cellular-recycling-increases-p.one_liner: Researchers discovered that disabling cells' autophagy systems dramatically increases yields of hard-to-manufacture drug-target proteins.

earths-missing-billion-years-of-geologic.title: Earth's missing billion years of geological history explained by subsurface processes
earths-missing-billion-years-of-geologic.one_liner: Scientists may have identified the mechanism explaining why Earth's geological record lacks evidence for over a billion years of history, pointing to deep crustal processes.

anthropics-wall-street-debut-marks-new-c.one_liner: Anthropic held its initial public offering, marking a significant milestone for AI-focused companies seeking institutional investment in mainstream capital markets.

claude-fable-52-solves-open-problems-in-.title: Claude Fable 5.2 solves open problems in black hole physics
claude-fable-52-solves-open-problems-in-.one_liner: Claude Fable 5.2 solved two previously open theoretical problems in black hole physics. First, it completed a complex calculation from 2003 about the Hawking-Page transition, showing it remains abrupt even in the quantum regime where spacetime lacks definite shape. Second, it found the exact limit of the simplest modular bootstrap technique used in quantum gravity research. Preprints were published November 17, 2026.
takeaways: Solved 20-year-old Hawking-Page transition calculation
Demonstrated sudden transition persists in quantum regime
Found exact limit of simplest modular bootstrap version
Both findings relate to holographic duality in quantum gravity; preprints published November 17, 2026

non-invasive-high-precision-independentl.title: Non-invasive high-precision independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized temporal interference stimulation
non-invasive-high-precision-independentl.one_liner: Researchers developed optimized temporal interference stimulation—a non-invasive technique using multiple kHz-range electric fields to achieve precise, steerable deep brain stimulation without implanted electrodes. Validation in humans showed the method can modulate hippocampal activity and enhance episodic memory accuracy, addressing limitations of surgical deep brain stimulation.
takeaways: Non-invasive deep brain stimulation using multiple kHz-range electric fields
Validated in humans; published in Nature Neuroscience (October 2023)
Successfully focused stimulation in hippocampus with minimal cortical exposure
Enhanced episodic memory accuracy in healthy humans

ai-discovers-critical-bugs-in-nginx-affe.title: AI discovers critical bugs in NGINX affecting 225 million websites
ai-discovers-critical-bugs-in-nginx-affe.one_liner: F5 released emergency patches for 10 vulnerabilities in NGINX on November 18, 2026, including two critical remote code execution flaws (CVSS 9.2) affecting approximately 225 million websites—about one-third of all websites. One bug had been in the code for at least 10 years. Researchers using AI tools discovered the flaws independently. No active exploitation has been reported; users should update to NGINX version 1.31.9 immediately.
takeaways: 10 vulnerabilities patched November 18, 2026
2 critical RCE flaws (CVSS 9.2) in HTTP/2 support
Affects ~225 million websites (one-third of all websites)
One bug in code for at least 10 years; no exploitation reported yet

ai-debt-collection-platform-creditnirvan.one_liner: Critical vulnerabilities in the CreditNirvana platform exposed millions of detailed records including emails, texts, credit reports, and call recordings.

us-measles-elimination-status-lost-as-en.one_liner: The United States has lost its measles elimination status as case numbers continue accelerating amid insufficient vaccination rates.

anthropic-prices-ipo-at-83-per-share-val.one_liner: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on November 18, 2026, above the initial range of $70–$78, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Amazon holds 15% and Google holds 14%. Major tech companies including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners agreed to purchase $26 billion in non-voting shares through private placement. Above initial range of $70–$78
$26 billion committed by seven major tech companies via private placement

critical-apache-roller-rce-flaw-under-ac.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE flaw under active exploitation with no authentication required
critical-apache-roller-rce-flaw-under-ac.one_liner: A critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-129448, CVSS 9.8) in Apache Roller is under active exploitation. The flaw stems from insecure deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint and affects versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. Exploitation occurs before authentication checks, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code. Users should upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later; interim mitigation includes disabling extension types.
takeaways: CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) actively exploited in the wild
Affects Apache Roller 4.0.0–6.1.4; insecure deserialization in XML-RPC
Unauthenticated RCE before authentication checks
Upgrade to 6.1.6+ or disable extension types in web.xml

astronomers-witness-star-engulfing-stell.one_liner: Astronomers have directly observed, possibly for the first time, a star consuming its stellar companion.

iran-and-us-escalate-tit-for-tat-strikes.title: Iran and U.S. escalate tit-for-tat strikes; Gulf states and tankers targeted
iran-and-us-escalate-tit-for-tat-strikes.one_liner: The U.S. and Iran escalated military strikes in the Persian Gulf region on November 18, 2026. The U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz in response to Iranian attacks on U.S. radar installations in Bahrain. Iran launched weapons in response, which Bahrain and Kuwait said they intercepted. A UAE state oil company ship (ADNOC) was struck, with one crew member missing and eleven injured. Yemen's Houthi militants targeted Saudi airports and financial centers. The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed the Middle East, leaving two U.S. carriers in the region.
takeaways: U.S. struck Qeshm Island November 18 in response to Iranian radar attacks
Iran targeted U.S. radar installation in Bahrain for third time in week
ADNOC ship struck in Strait of Hormuz; 1 missing, 11 injured
Houthi militants targeted Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Airport and Riyadh financial center

decade-old-nginx-http2-vulnerability-cve.title: Decade-old NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerability CVE-2026-123007 enables unauthenticated code execution
decade-old-nginx-http2-vulnerability-cve.one_liner: CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," is a critical flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support affecting all open-source releases from version 1.9.5 (September 2015) through 1.31.8 (October 2026). Unauthenticated remote attackers can execute code with NGINX worker permissions on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. CVSS score is 9.2. Fixed versions released November 18, 2026: NGINX Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7; NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1.
takeaways: CVE-2026-123007 (CVSS 9.2); in code since version 1.9.5 (September 2015)
Requires HTTP/2 enabled; unauthenticated RCE with worker privileges
Affects NGINX Open Source and Plus; fixed versions released November 18, 2026
ASLR bypass demonstrated; privilege escalation possible via second vector

putin-trump-and-xi-meet-in-trilateral-su.title: Putin, Trump and Xi meet in trilateral summit
putin-trump-and-xi-meet-in-trilateral-su.one_liner: The president of the United States arrived in China on November 18, 2026, and met with Chinese President Xi Jinping. A trilateral summit with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled for November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen. The president held an informal meeting with Putin on November 18, and indicated he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Before departing to China, he announced a major trade deal with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
takeaways: Arrived in China November 18, 2026
Trilateral summit with Xi Jinping and Putin scheduled November 19
Informal meeting with Putin held November 18
May meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un; major trade deal announced with Philippines
